A.explanation: P and Q both act on the box, so they cannot be a third-law pair, and they are not the same type since P is a contact normal force and Q is weight.

B.explanation: P and Q both act on the box, so they cannot be a third-law pair, and P is a contact force while Q is a gravitational force.

C.explanation: R and S both act on the Earth, so they cannot be a third-law pair, and R is a contact force while S is a gravitational force.

D.explanation: Q is the Earth pulling down on the box and S is the box pulling up on the Earth, so they act on different bodies, are opposite in direction and are both gravitational.

walkthrough: Identify the four forces from the diagram and stem: P is upward on the box from the ground, Q is downward on the box, while R is downward and S is upward on the Earth.

State the rule for a Newton third-law pair: the two forces must act on different bodies, be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, and be the same type of force such as both contact or both gravitational.
Reject pairs on the same body: P and Q cannot pair because both act on the box, and R and S cannot pair because both act on the Earth, even though each pair balances for the resting box.
Classify the types: P is the normal contact force on the box and R is the box pushing down in contact on the ground, so P pairs with R as contact forces.
Classify gravity: Q is the weight of the box, the gravitational pull of the Earth down on the box, so its pair must be the gravitational pull of the box up on the Earth, which is S.
This matches the statement that S is the equal and opposite force to Q and both are gravitational forces. This is option D.
